roots.story: The iron hills of the south-east coast were dug by small orc holds long before Aen, and their deepest pit is the reason Britadon digs wide and never deep. In the First Age the holds of these hills sank a shaft deeper than any other, the pit the orcs now call the Hollow, and in Volgan's war, when the Damned Spirits rose from beneath the mountains, something breathed out of the Hollow that the hill-orcs will not describe. The black boars of the hills fled first, out of the hills and down to the headlands, and the orcs who followed the boars lived; those who stayed by the pits did not. The survivors sealed the Hollow with slag and stone, and from that night come the hills' laws: no shaft may go deeper than the Brakgul measure, the iron is won from wide pits and shallow galleries, and nobody hunts the black boar, which the Brakgul clan holds saved it. Bredesk of the Brakgul, who brought the headland hold of Beriath under Fontadon's iron in 4A 1380, did it partly to own the headlands the boars had led the clans to, and the same caution made his heirs sell their iron by sea from 4A 1500 rather than send it through Goldoroth's lands. They took a seat at the Free Moot in 4A 1520 because they wanted friends in the hills if Goldoroth came. In 4A 1748 the Hollow is still sealed, Goldoroth's smiths would like to know how deep the coast's iron goes, and Britadon's chiefs answer that it goes exactly as deep as the measure.

sign.device: The Running Boar: a black boar running with white tusks bared, on iron-red, with a black hem.
sign.origin: When something breathed out of the Hollow in Volgan's war, the black boars of the hills ran first, down from the pits to the headlands, and the orcs who followed them lived. The Brakgul took the running boar as their clan's sign that night and painted it on the slag that sealed the Hollow, and since Bredesk joined the headland to Fontadon in 4A 1380 it has been sewn on the hold's banner and branded on its iron bars. No Brakgul hunts the black boar, and a boar seen running down from the hills is still reason enough to empty the pits.
sign.meaning: Follow the boar and live: the banner promises that Britadon's iron is won without waking what lies deep, and warns that the hold flees nothing else.

dynasties.name: The Brakgul iron-chiefs
dynasties.notable: Chiefs of the Brakgul clan who hold the iron and the ring at Fontadon until challenged.

events.name: The Hollow Sealed
events.summary: Something breathed out of the deepest pit of the south-east hills in Volgan's war; the orcs who followed the fleeing boars to the headlands lived, and they sealed the pit with slag and stone.

events.name: The Headland Joined
events.summary: Bredesk of the Brakgul brought Beriath under Fontadon's iron.

events.name: The Iron by Sea
events.summary: Britadon opened a sea trade in iron to the Dark Lands' harbours, so that it need not send its iron through Goldoroth's lands.

events.name: The Free Moot Joined
events.summary: Britadon's chief took a seat at the Free Moot of Dulundur, so that the coast would have friends in the iron hills if Goldoroth came for its iron.

rivalries.nature: The warkingdom wants the coast's iron under the Yoke.

countries.capitalReason: Fontadon is the hill hold above the richest iron of the south-east hills, close enough to the coast for the iron to go down to the sea.
countries.today: About fifty thousand orcs of the Iron Clans mine the south-east iron hills with Beriath and sell iron by sea. Britadon sits at the Free Moot and watches Goldoroth's border.

divergence.what: Britadon bows to the Iron Yoke.
divergence.consequence: Goldoroth gains the iron of the south-east coast and a harbour for it.

divergence.what: Britadon sells all its iron to the Accord.
divergence.consequence: Dondor's armouries are fed from the coast, and Goldoroth marks Britadon for its first campaign.

divergence.what: Goldoroth's smiths, or a hungry Britadon chief, unseal the Hollow for the iron below the measure.
divergence.consequence: Whatever breathed out of the Hollow before breathes out again, the south-east hills empty as the boars run, and the coast's iron is lost to everyone.

countries.name: Wild Lands

founding.story: The Wild Lands moor and the Doltu marsh are where broken clans go when no hold will have them, and they have never had a council. Men and orcs date the wild land from 4A 1500, when the clans of the moor agreed on the one rule they keep: the moor belongs to whoever stays through a winter, and the largest winter camp, at Zudertu, belongs to whoever is strongest there when the snow comes.

roots.story: The Wild Lands moor was a battlefield before it was a refuge. In the last years of the Buried Wars, about 3A 690, the free holds' last host was broken on the moor by the Necromancer's garrisons, and the survivors scattered into the Doltu marsh; for centuries afterwards no hold would settle a field that held so many dead, and the moor became the place where those whom no hold would have went to live. Exiles, clanless orcs, beaten chiefs and runaways made camps there, and the camps fought each other until 4A 1500, when the clans of the moor agreed on the one rule they keep: the land belongs to whoever stays through a winter. The rule shaped everything on the moor. Nobody is asked his clan at Zudertu; whoever holds the largest winter camp when the snow comes speaks for the moor until the thaw; and on the first snow the winter-holder plants a bare pole at Zudertu, and every band that means to stay the winter ties a strip of its old clan-cloth to it. A camp that grows too large splits, as Zudertu did in 4A 1690, because no band on the moor will live under one that has become a hold. In 4A 1748 the Wild Lands are the one place in the Dark Lands where anyone can start over, and every hold that pushes its outcasts onto the moor knows that one winter they may come back as a host.

sign.device: The Rag-Pole: a bare black pole hung with three streaming strips of red, white and yellow cloth, on moor-brown, with a black hem.
sign.origin: On the first snow of every winter the winter-holder of Zudertu plants a bare pole in the camp, and every band that means to stay ties a strip of its old clan-cloth to it, so that by midwinter the pole is a mass of torn colours from every hold in the Dark Lands. The custom began with the winter rule of 4A 1500, and when the moor's bands first went raiding together they carried a pole with a few strips on it, which is the sign sewn on the moor's banner. The three strips stand for all the clans that are no longer anyone's, and any band may tie on another.
sign.meaning: No clan and every clan: the rag-pole promises a winter's place to anyone who stays, and warns the holds that their outcasts have a banner of their own.

dynasties.name: The winter-holders of Zudertu
dynasties.notable: No chief rules the Wild Lands; whoever holds the winter camp at Zudertu when the snow comes speaks for the moor until the thaw.

events.name: The Field of the Last Host
events.summary: The free holds' last host of the Buried Wars was broken on the moor by the Necromancer's garrisons, and for centuries no hold would settle a field that held so many dead.

events.name: The Winter Rule
events.summary: The clans of the moor agreed that the land belongs to whoever stays through a winter.

events.name: The Doltu Clans
events.summary: Broken clans of the Doltu marsh came onto the moor after a flood and stayed the winter, and so stayed for good.

events.name: The Splitting of Zudertu
events.summary: The winter camp grew so large that it split into two camps that fought each other through the spring, as every hold of the Wild Lands does when it grows too big.

countries.capitalReason: Zudertu is the largest winter camp on the moor, where the ground is driest and the wind least cruel, held each winter by whoever is strongest there.
countries.today: About thirty thousand orcs of broken clans live on the Wild Lands moor and the Doltu marsh without a council. The land is held by whoever stays through a winter and contested by everyone else.

divergence.what: A strong chief holds Zudertu for many winters and makes the moor a hold.
divergence.consequence: The Wild Lands gain a council and a voice at the Free Moot, and lose the freedom that made them a refuge.

divergence.what: Goldoroth or Dondor settles the moor.
divergence.consequence: The broken clans are scattered again, and the Dark Lands lose the one place where anyone can start over.

divergence.what: The bands of the moor march together under the rag-pole against the hold that has driven the most outcasts onto it.
divergence.consequence: The Dark Lands learn that their outcasts are a host, the hold they march on must buy them off or fight them, and the moor gains a name it never wanted.

cities.name: Cocanoor
cities.legend: The Fire-Speakers of Cocanoor say the fire in the Warking's hall was taken from the mountain's mouth by the first Warking with his bare hand, and that a Warking who cannot hold his hand over it may be challenged.
cities.economy: Siege forges, iron of the arm, ash-glass and the tribute of the Iron Yoke.

cities.name: Notbuton
cities.legend: The folk of Notbuton say the first Brute-King's iron bar lies under the hall's hearth, and that the kingdom will stand as long as nobody digs it up.
cities.economy: Grain of the plain, iron, Leren trade across the straits and the beacon hills.

cities.name: Dontadur
cities.legend: The burghers of Dontadur say the first Leren ship to moor there was so heavy with silver that it sank at the quay, and that the town was built on what the divers brought up.
cities.economy: Iron of the Iron Road shipped north, Leren trade and the town moot.

cities.name: Lesderle
cities.legend: The orcs of the long valley say that if one of the Four Fires in the hall at Lesderle ever goes out, that valley will be lost within a year, and so a goblin is paid to sit by each one at night.
cities.economy: Iron of the four valleys, the Free Moot and its toll and iron prices.

cities.name: Notle
cities.legend: The sea orcs of Notle say the skull sunk with the iron bar when the Accord was sworn will rise again the day the Accord is broken.
cities.economy: Sea-orc ships, fishing, salt and the Salt Tithe.

cities.name: Doldes
cities.legend: The gate-orcs say Zugash built the gate-fort with the bones of the first caravan that refused his toll, and that the gate creaks whenever a caravan thinks of refusing.
cities.economy: The pass toll on every caravan, paid partly to Cocanoor.

cities.name: Zubudor
cities.legend: Caravan masters at Zubudor say the inns were barracks once and the orc chiefs still keep a spear behind every bar, which is why nobody starts a fight there.
cities.economy: Caravan inns on the Black Road, iron and the gorge toll.

cities.name: Dolido
cities.legend: The fen orcs say the hall on black piles stands on the drowned host of the Necromancer's levies, and that the piles were driven through them.
cities.economy: Eels, peat, bog-iron and the reed-council's hall.

cities.name: Holos
cities.legend: Orcs of the Black Road say the troll king's cave goes down further than any mine, and that the trolls who turned to stone in the sun stand in its mouth as guards.
cities.economy: Nothing that is traded; the troll silver left at the forest's edge.

cities.name: Burnikzig
cities.legend: The goblins say the great lamp in the hall of fire was lit from the volcano itself on the night the first Big Snik was chosen, and that the warrens are free only while it burns.
cities.economy: Powder, traps, small smithies and the warm caves' sulphur and saltpetre.

cities.name: Gollonlon
cities.legend: The forest-orcs say every chief of Gollonlon must fell a great tree with his own axe, and that the stumps round the hold are the chiefs who could not.
cities.economy: Timber and charcoal for the straits and the iron hills.

cities.name: Dobudo
cities.legend: The toll-gatherers of Dobudo say a ship that passes without paying will find the Dun Sea's current against it all the way home.
cities.economy: The Dun Sea tolls, fishing and the swing crown's bargains.

cities.name: Ozmath-Vesh
cities.legend: The thralls of the hall of ash say the hall has no door that a mortal can find from outside, and that those who leave it never find the way back in.
cities.economy: Nothing grows; the hall lives on what its thralls fish and what its pact-bargains bring.

cities.name: Maruunos
cities.legend: Woodcutters of the Dondor plain say the cairn-hall by the Giant River has a stone for every winter the giants have kept the line, and that nobody has ever seen the last one laid.
cities.economy: Hunting and gathering in the Giant Forest; the giants trade with nobody.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The ring
lawsAndCustoms.summary: An orc chief holds his hold, and the Warking his throne, until a stronger challenger breaks him in the ring; a chief broken in the ring is not killed if he yields, and may serve the one who broke him.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Iron Yoke
lawsAndCustoms.summary: A tributary hold of Goldoroth pays Cocanoor in iron each year and has its new chiefs confirmed by the Warking, but keeps its own ring and its own fire.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The blood-price of Dondor
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Dondor's law is the blood-price, set by the clan-moot, and a bar of iron is kept at every hearth and passed to the eldest as the house's oath.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The troll silver
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Silver left at the Troll Forest's edge buys a traveller or an envoy passage through it; caravans may not camp inside it, and armies that do are smashed by night.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The cairn-line
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The Borderline of Giants is not crossed and its cairns are not touched; whoever does either has the giants as an enemy.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The winter rule
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The moor belongs to whoever stays through a winter, and a hold that grows too big splits.
